prompt: The table shows $120$ students by grade and whether they have a part-time job. A student is chosen at random. Given that the student is a SENIOR, what is the probability they have a job?
hint: The words "given that the student is a senior" shrink the group you are choosing from. Which part of the table is left?

hints.text: The words "given that the student is a senior" shrink the group you are choosing from. Which part of the table is left?
Only the senior row matters. It has $70$ seniors, and $45$ of them have a job, so write $\frac{45}{70}$ and simplify.

explanation: Conditioning on "senior" means the sample space is no longer all $120$ students, only the $70$ seniors.
Within that row, $45$ seniors have a part-time job, so those are the favorable outcomes.
The conditional probability is $P(\text{job} \mid \text{senior}) = \frac{45}{70} = \frac{9}{14}$, which is about $0.643$.

alternativeExplanations.title: With the formula
steps: Compare: $P(\text{job}) = \frac{75}{120} = 0.625$, so seniors are a little more likely than students overall to have a job.
